## Simple explanation

Data engineering is the work of building and maintaining systems that make
data available, organized, and reliable for applications, analytics, and
machine learning.

## Technical explanation

Data engineering includes ingestion, transformation, storage, orchestration,
quality checks, access control, and observability. Systems may process
data in batches or streams and can use warehouses, lakes, databases, and
message brokers.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Machine-learning systems depend on data that is correctly collected,
versioned, transformed, and delivered. Weak data foundations can cause
training-serving inconsistencies, leakage, unreliable evaluation, and
production failures.

## How it works

A data system ingests sources, validates and transforms records, stores
them in suitable formats, and schedules or streams outputs to downstream
consumers. Monitoring and lineage help teams investigate where data came
from and how it changed.

## Practical example

A data pipeline can collect labeled support conversations, remove
disallowed fields, validate schemas, create training examples, and publish
a versioned dataset for model training.

## Common misconceptions

- Data engineering is not only moving data between databases.
- A successful pipeline run does not guarantee that its data is accurate
  or appropriate for a model.
- Data quality and governance are engineering concerns, not optional
  cleanup steps.
